text: A SOC wants new high-severity Microsoft Sentinel incidents to be assigned to the Tier 2 queue and moved to a consistent status before any external response workflow runs. Which TWO actions can an automation rule handle directly as part of incident management?

choices.text: Assign the incident to a designated owner
Change the incident status when conditions match
Query an external threat-intelligence API for enrichment
Run a forensic PowerShell script on the affected endpoint
Create a memory image from the affected device

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel automation rules can perform built-in incident-management actions such as assigning an owner, changing status, tagging, or closing an incident, and they can also call a playbook when more complex orchestration is needed. External enrichment and endpoint scripting are examples of work better suited to a playbook or another response capability. The key distinction is that the first two actions are native incident-handling actions of the automation rule itself.

text: An analyst needs Microsoft Sentinel to open a ticket in an external service-management platform and then post investigation details to a collaboration channel whenever a qualifying incident is created. What should the analyst build for this cross-service workflow?

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel playbooks are workflows built on Azure Logic Apps and are intended to automate and orchestrate response across services through connectors, conditions, and actions. A workbook visualizes data, and a hunting query searches telemetry; neither performs a multi-step external workflow. A device group controls scope and automation behavior for Defender for Endpoint devices rather than coordinating Sentinel response tasks.

text: An organization wants Defender for Endpoint remediation actions on standard user devices to run automatically, while actions on a sensitive server group should require security-team approval. Which configuration provides that control?

choices.text: Set different automation levels on Defender for Endpoint device groups
Create separate Microsoft Sentinel workbooks for the device categories
Use different Microsoft Purview audit-retention policies by device type
Apply different Microsoft Sentinel hunting queries to each device category

communityTop.text: Defender for Endpoint device groups can be configured with automation levels that determine whether remediation actions are taken automatically or wait for approval. That makes device groups the control point for applying different AIR behavior to different device populations. Workbooks, Purview retention, and hunting queries do not govern whether endpoint remediation actions execute automatically.

text: A security engineer is configuring the Windows Security Events via AMA connector for Microsoft Sentinel and needs to control which Windows event-log records are collected and where they are sent. Which object should be configured?

communityTop.text: Windows Security Events via Azure Monitor Agent uses a data collection rule to define event sources, destinations, and the data flow that sends selected Windows events to the Log Analytics workspace. A workbook is for visualization, while device isolation and threat analytics address response and threat context. The DCR is therefore the configuration object that controls this ingestion path.

text: A Microsoft Sentinel detection must evaluate newly ingested events with the lowest built-in rule latency because a one-minute delay materially affects containment. Which analytics rule type best fits this requirement?

choices.text: A scheduled analytics rule with a daily interval
A workbook query pinned to the SOC dashboard

communityTop.text: Near-real-time (NRT) analytics rules are designed for up-to-the-minute detection and run their queries at one-minute intervals over recently ingested events. Scheduled rules are more flexible but are not the lowest-latency built-in choice for this requirement. Workbooks and hunting queries can expose suspicious data, but they do not provide the same continuously evaluated NRT detection behavior.

text: A threat hunter has a validated Advanced Hunting query in Microsoft Defender XDR and wants the query to run automatically, generate alerts when it matches, and optionally take response actions. What should be created?

communityTop.text: Defender XDR custom detections are built from Advanced Hunting queries and can run automatically at configured intervals to generate alerts and take response actions when matches occur. A workbook visualizes data, a device filter only changes how assets are viewed, and an eDiscovery case manages investigation content. The requirement to operationalize a hunting query into repeatable detection points directly to a custom detection rule.

text: A team keeps large volumes of security telemetry in the Microsoft Sentinel data lake tier. It wants a scheduled KQL process to query that data and place selected results into the analytics tier for faster downstream use. Which feature should it configure?

communityTop.text: A Microsoft Sentinel KQL job runs a KQL query against data in the data lake tier and writes or promotes the resulting data into the analytics tier, either once or on a schedule. A workbook presents query results but does not perform that tier-to-tier processing. Device groups and Purview audit searches serve different endpoint and compliance investigation purposes.

text: A built-in Microsoft Sentinel analytics rule queries the SecurityEvent table, but events arriving through a Windows Forwarded Events connector never match the rule even though forwarding is healthy. What is the most likely explanation?

choices.text: Forwarded events are written to WindowsEvent instead of SecurityEvent
The connector stores forwarded events only in Defender XDR incidents
Windows Event Forwarding suppresses all events used by analytics rules
The SecurityEvent table accepts only events collected from Linux hosts

communityTop.text: Microsoft documentation distinguishes the ingestion paths: Windows Security Events via AMA writes supported events to SecurityEvent, while the Windows Forwarded Events connector writes forwarded events to WindowsEvent. A built-in rule that only queries SecurityEvent therefore will not see those forwarded records unless its query is adapted. The issue is the destination table, not broken forwarding or a Linux-only limitation.

text: An analyst is investigating suspicious behavior on one endpoint and needs a chronological view of observed events, associated alerts, process relationships, and MITRE ATT&CK techniques for that device. Which Defender for Endpoint view should be opened first?

communityTop.text: The Defender for Endpoint device timeline provides a chronological view of events and associated alerts observed on a device and supports investigation features such as process trees and MITRE ATT&CK context. Vulnerability recommendations focus on exposure reduction, while email entities and workbook galleries are different investigation or visualization surfaces. The timeline is the direct view for reconstructing endpoint activity over time.

text: A security analyst must connect to a compromised endpoint immediately, run investigative commands, collect forensic artifacts, and take remediation actions without waiting for an interactive user session. Which capability is designed for this?

communityTop.text: Defender for Endpoint live response provides an on-demand remote shell to an onboarded device so analysts can run commands, collect forensic data, retrieve files, run scripts, and take immediate response actions. Threat analytics supplies threat intelligence and exposure context, while Purview Audit and workbooks do not create a remote response session to the endpoint.

text: During an endpoint investigation, the SOC wants a downloadable package that captures information about the device state so analysts can examine evidence outside the live portal session. Which Defender for Endpoint response action best matches this need?

communityTop.text: Collect investigation package gathers a downloadable package from the device to help analysts understand its current state and the tools or techniques involved in an attack. Restricting app execution and automatic attack disruption are containment-oriented actions, while a hunting bookmark preserves investigation context in Sentinel. The requirement is evidence collection for offline examination, which is the purpose of the investigation package.

text: An investigation asks who changed a Microsoft 365 administrative setting and when the change occurred. The analyst needs a record of user and administrator activity rather than the content of messages or files. Which tool is the best starting point?

communityTop.text: Microsoft Purview Audit records and exposes user and administrator activities across Microsoft 365 services and is designed to answer questions about who performed an action and when. eDiscovery content search is the closer distractor because it searches stored messages and files, not the activity record itself. Sentinel notebooks and endpoint live response address hunting and device investigation rather than Microsoft 365 audit history.

text: A phishing investigation needs to locate messages and related files containing a distinctive campaign phrase across Exchange mailboxes, OneDrive accounts, and SharePoint sites. Which Microsoft Purview capability best fits this evidence search?

communityTop.text: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery can search content across Microsoft 365 locations such as Exchange mailboxes, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams-backed locations, and other supported services. Purview Audit is the tempting alternative, but it searches activity records rather than the actual message or file content being sought. Endpoint timelines and Sentinel NRT rules address different telemetry and detection use cases.

text: A SOC is investigating a suspected pass-the-ticket attack against on-premises Active Directory accounts and wants identity-focused detections for lateral movement techniques. Which Microsoft security product is most directly aligned to this investigation?

communityTop.text: Microsoft Defender for Identity monitors identity-related activity in environments that include on-premises Active Directory and provides alerts for techniques such as suspected pass-the-ticket and other lateral-movement behaviors. Defender for Cloud Apps focuses on cloud application risk, Defender for Office 365 on email and collaboration threats, and eDiscovery on content investigation. The attack described is fundamentally an identity and directory-service problem.

text: Microsoft Defender XDR confirms an active attack involving a compromised endpoint and a compromised user account. Which TWO automated disruption actions are designed to directly interrupt those attacker footholds?

choices.text: Isolate the compromised device from most network traffic
Disable the compromised user to prevent further sign-in
Collect an investigation package from the endpoint
Export the incident to a workbook for visualization
Search Microsoft Purview Audit for administrator activity

communityTop.text: Automatic attack disruption can isolate a compromised device and disable a compromised user account to cut off active attacker access and reduce lateral movement. Collecting an investigation package is useful evidence gathering, but it does not itself interrupt the foothold. Workbook visualization and Purview Audit searches support investigation and reporting rather than directly containing the compromised device or identity.

text: A hunter wants to query Microsoft Defender XDR telemetry specifically for process creation and related process events observed on onboarded endpoints. Which Advanced Hunting table is the best starting point?

communityTop.text: DeviceProcessEvents contains process creation and related process events from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, making it the correct table for examining executions, command lines, and process relationships. DeviceNetworkEvents focuses on network connections, DeviceFileEvents on file-system activity, and DeviceRegistryEvents on registry changes. Choosing the table that matches the event type is a core Advanced Hunting skill.

text:
A hunter runs the following KQL query against endpoint process telemetry. What does the query return?

DeviceProcessEvents | summarize Executions=count() by bin(Timestamp, 1h)

choices.text: A count of process events grouped into one-hour time buckets
The single most common process name for the previous hour
A list of devices sorted by the time of their latest process event
Every process event with its timestamp rounded to the nearest hour

communityTop.text: The summarize operator aggregates rows, count() counts the rows in each group, and bin(Timestamp, 1h) places timestamps into one-hour buckets. The result is therefore one row per hourly bucket with the number of matching process events in that period. Rounding a timestamp alone would not aggregate rows, and finding a most-common process or latest device event would require different grouping and sorting logic.

text: An analyst has a hypothesis about credential misuse and wants to run a query proactively across Sentinel data, review matches, and refine the idea before deciding whether it deserves continuous alerting. Which feature best fits this first step?

choices.text: A Defender for Endpoint device isolation action

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel hunting queries support proactive, analyst-driven searches before, during, and after incidents, making them appropriate for testing a hypothesis and reviewing matches. An analytics rule is the better next step once the logic should run continuously and generate detections. Device isolation is a response action, and a retention policy controls how long data is kept rather than how it is hunted.

text: A newly reported campaign is affecting organizations in the same sector. The SOC wants Microsoft-provided analysis of the tracked threat, related incidents, impacted assets in its environment, and recommended mitigation actions. Which Defender XDR capability should it use?

communityTop.text: Defender XDR Threat analytics provides reports on tracked and emerging threats, including attack-chain context, related incidents, impacted assets, exposure information, hunting guidance, and recommended actions. Device inventory lists assets but does not provide the campaign analysis, while eDiscovery and data collection rules serve content investigation and ingestion configuration. The requirement is threat-specific intelligence enriched with the organization’s own exposure.

text: An incident begins with one compromised account. The analyst wants an interactive graph showing the current impact and possible propagation paths toward critical assets so the team can estimate how far the breach could spread. Which capability best matches this goal?

choices.text: Blast radius analysis powered by Microsoft Sentinel graph
A Microsoft Sentinel workbook time chart
A Microsoft Purview audit retention policy
A Defender for Endpoint software inventory view

communityTop.text: Blast radius analysis uses Microsoft Sentinel graph infrastructure to visualize current impact and possible future propagation paths from a compromised entity toward important targets. A workbook can chart data but does not provide the same relationship-based reachability view. Audit retention and software inventory answer different compliance and asset questions, so they do not model how an attacker could traverse connected identities and resources.

text: A sanctioned administration tool repeatedly generates a known-benign Defender for Endpoint alert. The SOC wants matching alerts removed from the alert queue and prevented from creating incidents, while still retaining the underlying alert data for hunting. Which alert tuning action best fits?

choices.text: Hide the alert when the defined evidence conditions match
Resolve the alert and its related incident after creation
Convert the alert into a Microsoft Sentinel workbook item
Disable automated investigation and response for the device

communityTop.text: The Hide alert action suppresses matching Defender for Endpoint alerts and prevents them from creating incidents, while the alert data remains available in hunting tables such as AlertInfo and AlertEvidence. Resolve alert instead creates the matching alert and related incident in a resolved state. Disabling automated investigation changes response behavior, not whether the known-benign alert appears in the queue.

text: A Tier 1 analyst must view Microsoft Sentinel data and incidents, assign incidents to owners, change incident status, and add investigation notes. The analyst must not create analytics rules or modify Sentinel resources. Which role is the best fit?

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel Responder includes Reader permissions and adds the ability to manage incidents, which matches assignment, status changes, and investigation handling. Contributor goes further by allowing creation and editing of Sentinel resources such as analytics rules, so it grants more access than required. Reader cannot manage incidents, and Playbook Operator is focused on manually running playbooks.

text: A Microsoft Sentinel workspace ingests standard Syslog messages from Linux servers and Common Event Format (CEF) events from network security appliances through Azure Monitor Agent. Which TWO tables should an analyst expect to query for those records?

choices.text: Syslog for the standard Syslog records
SecurityEvent for all Linux and appliance records
OfficeActivity for the standard Syslog records

communityTop.text: With the Syslog via AMA connector, standard Syslog records are stored in the Syslog table. CEF via AMA parses security appliance events into CommonSecurityLog. SecurityEvent is associated with Windows security-event ingestion, DeviceNetworkEvents is Defender endpoint telemetry, and OfficeActivity contains Microsoft 365 activity rather than Linux or appliance Syslog data.

text: A legacy security application writes one-line records to a rotating text file on a Linux server. No built-in Microsoft Sentinel connector exists for the application, but the SOC needs selected file records ingested into a queryable custom table. Which ingestion approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Custom Logs via AMA with a data collection rule
Windows Security Events via AMA with a security event set
Microsoft Defender XDR alert tuning with a file condition
A Microsoft Sentinel workbook that reads the file directly

communityTop.text: Custom Logs via AMA is designed to collect text-file logs from applications on Windows or Linux and send selected records through a data collection rule into a custom Log Analytics table. Windows Security Events is for Windows event logs, not arbitrary application files. Alert tuning suppresses expected alerts, and a workbook visualizes data that is already queryable rather than ingesting a local file.

text: The SOC wants Microsoft Sentinel to automatically compare supported domain, IP, and URL threat indicators with ingested security logs and create high-fidelity detections when matches occur. Which built-in capability most directly provides this matching?

choices.text: Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence Analytics rule
A Microsoft Sentinel workbook with threat charts
A Defender for Endpoint device inventory filter
A Microsoft Purview Audit search template

communityTop.text: The Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence Analytics rule is a built-in Sentinel matching rule that correlates supported threat indicators such as domains, IP addresses, and URLs with compatible ingested logs. A workbook can visualize threat data but does not continuously perform the matching. Device inventory and Purview Audit serve endpoint inventory and Microsoft 365 audit investigation rather than indicator correlation.

text: A scheduled Microsoft Sentinel analytics rule detects suspicious sign-ins, but incidents show only raw query columns and do not expose the affected account and IP address as investigation entities. What should the security engineer configure in the rule?

choices.text: Entity mapping from query fields to account and IP entities
A longer query scheduling interval to enrich each result
A workbook parameter for the account and IP columns
A data collection rule transformation that removes unused fields

communityTop.text: Entity mapping tells Microsoft Sentinel which query-result fields represent entities such as accounts, hosts, or IP addresses. Mapped entities then appear in alerts and incidents so analysts can investigate relationships and context more effectively. Scheduling intervals and workbook parameters do not create incident entities, while an ingestion transformation changes stored data rather than the alert entity model.

text: A built-in Microsoft Sentinel anomaly rule is useful but too sensitive for one environment. The team wants to change its thresholds, compare the adjusted behavior during testing, and then promote the tuned version to production. What should the team do?

choices.text: Duplicate the anomaly rule and tune the duplicate
Edit the original out-of-box anomaly rule in place
Replace the anomaly rule with a workbook visualization
Disable User and Entity Behavior Analytics for the workspace

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel does not let analysts modify the original out-of-box anomaly configuration directly. The supported approach is to duplicate the anomaly rule, adjust the duplicate's thresholds or parameters, compare its performance during testing, and promote that tuned copy when it behaves as intended. A workbook only visualizes results, and disabling UEBA would remove useful behavioral context rather than tune this rule.

text: A security engineer creates a Defender for Endpoint custom data collection rule that captures nearly every process event. Microsoft recommends targeting only a small pilot group first. What is the primary reason for that recommendation?

choices.text: Comprehensive collection can generate very high event volumes per device
Custom data collection works only on devices in evaluation mode
The collected events cannot be queried until every device is targeted
Pilot targeting is required before Defender XDR can create incidents

communityTop.text: Custom data collection can produce very large telemetry volumes, and Microsoft specifically cautions that collecting all matching events can quickly approach the per-device event limit. A small pilot lets the team validate usefulness and volume before broad deployment. The feature is not limited to evaluation devices, and neither query availability nor incident creation requires targeting the entire fleet first.

text: A security engineer wants to reduce common Office-based intrusion paths on Windows endpoints by blocking behaviors such as Office applications creating child processes. Which Defender for Endpoint control family should the engineer configure?

communityTop.text: Attack surface reduction rules are preventive endpoint controls that block specific behaviors commonly abused during attacks, including Office applications launching child processes. Alert tuning affects how expected alerts are handled after detection, and hunting queries search existing telemetry. Purview retention controls data lifecycle, so none of those alternatives directly blocks the risky endpoint behavior described.

text: An incident contains suspicious files, processes, IP addresses, and email artifacts. The analyst wants one Defender XDR view that shows supported evidence with verdicts such as Malicious, Suspicious, or Clean and also shows remediation status. Which incident tab should be used?

communityTop.text: The Evidence and Response tab brings together supported suspicious entities from the incident and shows their investigation verdicts and remediation status. It also provides access to pending remediation actions when applicable. Asset inventory and Secure Score focus on environment posture, while Threat analytics provides campaign intelligence rather than the incident-specific evidence and remediation view.

text: A SOC handles several investigations related to the same internal red-team exercise. Analysts want to label those incidents so the queue can later be filtered to that exercise without changing the detection logic. Which incident-management feature should they use?

communityTop.text: Incident tags add contextual labels to incidents and can later be used as filtering criteria in the incident queue, which is ideal for grouping a known exercise or campaign. Severity expresses urgency rather than arbitrary grouping. Alert tuning changes how matching alerts are handled, and threat indicators represent potentially malicious observables rather than case-management labels.

text: Several users received a phishing message that was later confirmed malicious. The analyst needs to find matching delivered messages across the organization, inspect message details, and initiate remediation actions on the affected mail. Which Defender for Office 365 capability best fits?

communityTop.text: Threat Explorer is built for near-real-time investigation and response to email threats, including locating delivered malicious messages and initiating remediation such as deleting or moving affected mail. A Sentinel workbook can visualize ingested data but is not the primary email-remediation surface. Endpoint timelines and retention labels solve device-investigation and information-lifecycle problems instead.

text: An OAuth application has unusual tenant-wide permissions and was recently granted admin consent. The analyst wants to review the app's granted permissions, consent activity, and related cloud activity before deciding whether the app is risky. Which capability should be used?

choices.text: OAuth app investigation in Defender for Cloud Apps
Device inventory in Defender for Endpoint

communityTop.text: Defender for Cloud Apps provides an OAuth app investigation experience that exposes granted permissions, consent activity, usage, and related activities so analysts can evaluate suspicious applications. Defender for Endpoint device inventory focuses on endpoints, while Sentinel DCRs configure ingestion. Secure Score recommends posture improvements but is not the detailed OAuth consent and activity investigation surface.

text: A user account is confirmed compromised and the attacker may still have valid cloud sessions. Which TWO containment actions most directly cut off both new sign-ins and existing refresh-token-backed access?

choices.text: Block or disable the user account
Add the incident to a Sentinel workbook
Create a new device group for the user's workstation

communityTop.text: Disabling or blocking the account prevents new sign-ins, while revoking sessions invalidates refresh tokens so existing cloud sessions must reauthenticate. Together they address both future and already-established access. Audit retention and workbooks support investigation and reporting, and a device group changes endpoint administration scope rather than directly containing the compromised cloud identity.

text: An investigation suggests a malicious application is making unauthorized calls to Microsoft Graph. The analyst needs an audit trail of HTTP requests that Microsoft Graph received and processed for the tenant. Which data source is designed for this purpose?

communityTop.text: Microsoft Graph activity logs provide an audit trail of HTTP requests received and processed by Microsoft Graph for a tenant, including request-related fields useful for investigating application activity. An endpoint timeline records device telemetry, SecurityEvent stores Windows security events, and eDiscovery content search locates content in Microsoft 365 rather than tracing Graph API requests.

text: An automated investigation recommends remediation actions against devices, identities, and email, but the organization requires analyst approval before those actions execute. Where should the analyst review and approve or reject the pending actions?

choices.text: The Defender XDR threat analytics dashboard
The Microsoft Purview Audit search page

communityTop.text: The unified Action center centralizes remediation actions generated across devices, email and collaboration content, and identities. When automation is configured to require approval, analysts can review pending actions there and approve or reject them. Workbooks, threat analytics, and Purview Audit provide visualization, threat context, and audit searching rather than approval workflow for AIR remediation.

text: A hunter has suspicious process executions in DeviceProcessEvents and wants to correlate them with outbound connections in DeviceNetworkEvents using the shared DeviceId value. Which KQL operator is specifically intended to combine rows from the two tables on that matching key?

communityTop.text: The KQL join operator combines rows from two tabular expressions based on a matching key such as DeviceId, which is exactly what is needed to correlate process and network telemetry. summarize aggregates rows, project selects or renames columns, and extend adds calculated columns. Those operators are useful in hunts but do not by themselves combine records from two tables on a shared identifier.

text: A workspace retains a very large volume of inexpensive raw telemetry, but analysts repeatedly run month-long hunts that need only hourly aggregate counts. The team wants the aggregates precomputed into an Analytics-plan custom table for faster queries. Which feature should it configure?

choices.text: A Defender XDR alert tuning rule

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel summary rules run aggregation queries in the background and store the summarized results in custom tables using the Analytics plan. This improves performance for repeated long-range queries while allowing verbose raw logs to remain in lower-cost tiers. Alert tuning, retention labels, and incident tasks do not create precomputed security aggregates for hunting.

text: A threat hunter needs a reusable investigation that combines KQL results with Python analysis, visualizations, and iterative exploration that is more complex than a single portal query. Which Microsoft Sentinel capability is the best fit?

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel notebooks provide an interactive environment for complex hunts that can combine queries, Python code, analysis libraries, visualizations, and reusable investigative workflows. Automation rules orchestrate incident handling, tags classify cases, and data collection rules govern ingestion. None of those provides the same exploratory analysis environment for a multi-step hunt.

text:
A hunter wants to return only PowerShell process events whose command line contains the string "-enc", and then display only Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, and ProcessCommandLine. Which query shape best meets the requirement?

DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName =~ "powershell.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-enc" | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

choices.text: Filter matching rows first, then project the required columns
Aggregate all process events into hourly buckets before filtering
Join every process row to network telemetry before selecting fields
Extend each row with a constant value and return every column

communityTop.text: The where clause filters the process telemetry to PowerShell rows whose command line contains the target string, and project then limits the output to the four requested columns. summarize would aggregate data rather than preserve individual matches, and join is unnecessary because only one table is required. extend can add calculated fields but would not satisfy the request to return only the selected columns.

text: A SOC manager wants the on-call team to receive email only when new High-severity incidents are created from selected Defender detection sources. Which configuration most directly meets the requirement?

choices.text: Create a Defender XDR incident email notification rule filtered by severity and source
Create a Sentinel workbook that displays only High-severity incident records
Create an alert tuning rule that hides every alert below High severity
Create a Defender for Endpoint device group for the on-call analysts

communityTop.text: Microsoft Defender XDR incident email notification rules can target recipients and filter notifications by severity and detection or service source, which directly fits the requirement. A workbook only visualizes data that already exists and does not send incident notifications. Alert tuning changes alert handling, while device groups scope endpoint access and automation rather than email delivery.

text: A SOC needs 60 days of fast interactive access for analytics rules and hunting, but compliance requires the same table to remain retained for 5 years at lower cost after that period. Which TWO settings best satisfy the requirement?

choices.text: Keep the table in the Analytics tier with 60 days of analytics retention
Set total retention to 5 years so older data remains in the data lake
Move the table immediately to the Data Lake tier with no analytics retention
Configure a workbook to export the table to local files every 60 days
Extend Defender XDR advanced hunting retention to 5 years for the table

communityTop.text: Analytics retention keeps the recent 60-day window available to high-performance Sentinel features such as analytics rules and threat hunting. Extending total retention to 5 years keeps older data in the lower-cost data lake after it ages out of analytics retention. Moving the table fully to the Data Lake tier would stop real-time analytics on that table, while a workbook and Defender XDR retention do not implement this Sentinel table-retention design.

text: An analyst needs an interactive security dashboard with KQL-backed charts, tables, and a time-range parameter so shift leads can monitor trends without creating detections. Which Sentinel capability should be used?

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel workbooks are designed to visualize and monitor connected security data through queries, charts, tables, parameters, and other interactive elements. A scheduled analytics rule generates detections, a data collection rule controls ingestion, and an automation rule handles incident workflow. Those controls solve different problems and do not provide the requested interactive monitoring dashboard.

text: A Sentinel workspace ingests a costly table that has not been used by detections in the last month. The team wants Microsoft-generated guidance on whether to add useful detections, change the table plan, or stop unnecessary ingestion without reducing security coverage. Which feature should the team review?

communityTop.text: SOC optimization analyzes Sentinel usage and coverage to surface actionable data-value and coverage recommendations, including adding detections, changing eligible table plans, or reducing ingestion that provides little security value. Secure Score measures posture rather than Sentinel ingestion value. Purview and endpoint exposure features address different security domains and do not produce these Sentinel-specific optimization recommendations.

text: A security engineer must ingest Azure subscription control-plane events into Microsoft Sentinel using the current supported pipeline and wants a scalable way to configure multiple subscriptions. Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use the Azure Activity connector with diagnostic settings and Azure Policy where needed
Use Windows Security Events via AMA on every Azure virtual machine
Use Defender XDR custom detection rules to copy control-plane events into Sentinel
Use a Sentinel workbook to poll each subscription and store the results

communityTop.text: The current Azure Activity connector uses the diagnostic-settings pipeline to send subscription control-plane activity into the Sentinel workspace, and policy can be used to apply configuration at scale. Windows Security Events collects operating-system security logs rather than Azure control-plane operations. Custom detections and workbooks consume existing telemetry; they do not replace the supported ingestion pipeline.

text: A commercial threat-intelligence provider exposes a TAXII 2.x collection containing STIX indicators. The SOC wants those indicators ingested into Microsoft Sentinel through a supported connector. Which connector should it configure?

communityTop.text: The Threat Intelligence - TAXII connector is specifically designed to ingest STIX threat indicators from TAXII 2.x servers into Microsoft Sentinel. Azure Activity carries Azure control-plane events, the Defender XDR incidents connector synchronizes security incidents and alerts, and Windows Security Events via AMA ingests Windows event logs. None of those alternatives consumes a TAXII threat-intelligence feed.

text: A detection engineer wants to compare the MITRE ATT&CK techniques covered by active Sentinel scheduled and NRT rules with techniques that could be covered by available but not yet configured detections. Which Sentinel view is designed for this analysis?

choices.text: The MITRE ATT&CK coverage matrix with simulated rules
The Incident queue grouped by owner and severity
The Action center filtered to pending remediation
The Defender for Endpoint device inventory

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel's MITRE ATT&CK page visualizes coverage from active scheduled and NRT analytics rules and can also simulate coverage from available detections that are not yet configured. The incident queue and Action center are operational response views, and device inventory is an endpoint asset view. They do not compare active versus potential ATT&CK technique coverage.

text: A scheduled Sentinel analytics rule repeatedly detects the same account and host during one attack and creates many closely related alerts. The SOC wants those matching alerts represented together as one actionable incident when possible. What should the engineer configure?

choices.text: Alert grouping based on matching mapped entities
Event grouping to create a separate alert for every result
Rule suppression that stops all query execution for 24 hours
A workbook parameter containing the account and host names

communityTop.text: Alert grouping can combine related alerts from a scheduled analytics rule into a single incident using matching mapped entities and a defined time frame. Event grouping controls how query results become alerts, not how alerts are grouped into incidents. Suppression stops the rule from running for a period and can hide later activity, while workbook parameters affect visualization only.

text: A Defender for Cloud workload-protection alert reports suspicious activity on an Azure virtual machine. The analyst needs the affected resource, alert details, severity, and Microsoft-recommended remediation steps before taking action. Which view should the analyst investigate first?

choices.text: The Defender for Cloud security alert details
The Defender XDR email notification settings
The Microsoft Purview eDiscovery case list

communityTop.text: Defender for Cloud security alert details provide the affected resource, supporting alert information, severity, and recommended remediation guidance for workload-protection detections. Workbooks are for visualization, email-notification settings control message delivery, and eDiscovery cases search and preserve Microsoft 365 content. Those views do not provide the workload alert investigation context requested.

text: An analyst is investigating one authentication attempt from an anonymous IP address. The analyst needs details such as the application, device, location, Conditional Access result, and risk level for that specific attempt rather than the user's accumulated account risk. Which report is the best fit?

communityTop.text: The Risky sign-ins report focuses on individual authentication attempts and includes investigation fields such as application, device, location, Conditional Access information, and sign-in risk. The Risky users report summarizes risk at the identity level across detections and sign-ins. Endpoint inventory and Purview Audit serve device and Microsoft 365 activity investigations rather than this specific sign-in-risk question.

text: A compromised identity appears in alerts from several Microsoft security products. The analyst wants one chronological view of that user's impacted alerts, directory changes, cloud-app activity, and device logons to reconstruct the sequence. Which view should be used?

choices.text: The identity entity Timeline tab in Microsoft Defender
The Sentinel data connector health workbook

communityTop.text: The identity entity Timeline tab aggregates identity-related activity and alerts from integrated Microsoft security products into chronological order, including directory activity, cloud-app events, device logons, and impacted alerts. The Action center focuses on remediation actions, while connector health and retention pages address telemetry and data governance rather than reconstructing a user's activity sequence.

text: A Defender incident contains dozens of alerts across users and devices. Before deep investigation, the analyst wants an AI-generated overview of when the attack started, the likely starting asset, the attack timeline, involved assets, and indicators of compromise. Which embedded capability is intended for this?

communityTop.text: Security Copilot can generate an incident summary directly in Microsoft Defender, including the attack start, starting asset when known, timeline, involved assets, indicators of compromise, and suggested follow-up prompts. A Sentinel summary rule preaggregates telemetry for querying. Alert tuning reduces noise, and Content search finds Microsoft 365 content; neither produces the requested AI incident overview.

text: A SOC manager wants every analyst on every shift to follow and record the same triage and containment checklist for a recurring Sentinel incident type, while still allowing analysts to mark each step complete. Which capability best meets the requirement?

communityTop.text: Incident tasks provide a trackable checklist directly on an incident so analysts can follow standardized triage, investigation, and response steps and mark them complete. Tasks can also be added manually or generated through automation. Bookmarks preserve interesting hunting results, device groups scope endpoint permissions and automation, and retention labels govern information lifecycle rather than response workflow.

text: An analyst confirms that a workstation is actively attempting lateral movement. The analyst wants to cut the device off from normal network communication while keeping Defender for Endpoint able to monitor and manage the device. Which response action is designed for this?

choices.text: Add an indicator for the device name

communityTop.text: The Isolate device action disconnects a compromised endpoint from normal network access while retaining the Defender for Endpoint service connectivity needed for continued monitoring and management, subject to network configuration such as VPN design. Collecting an investigation package gathers artifacts but does not contain traffic. A scan checks files, and an indicator based on a device name is not the containment action described.

text: A phishing alert, a compromised-user alert, and a suspicious endpoint-process alert occur minutes apart and involve the same employee. Which TWO Defender XDR capabilities most directly help an analyst understand them as one multi-stage attack?

choices.text: Automatic correlation of related alerts into a shared incident
The attack story graph linking related users, devices, mailboxes, and alerts
A Purview retention label applied to the employee mailbox
A Secure Score recommendation for endpoint hardening
An Action center filter that shows only completed remediation actions

communityTop.text: Defender XDR correlates related alerts from different security sources into incidents so analysts do not have to assemble the attack story manually. The attack story graph then visualizes how alerts and entities such as users, devices, and mailboxes relate and evolve over time. Retention labels, Secure Score, and Action center filtering serve governance, posture, and remediation tracking rather than cross-domain attack correlation.

text: A phishing message was delivered to several Exchange Online mailboxes before Microsoft had enough evidence to classify it as malicious. New intelligence identifies it 2 hours later, and the organization wants Defender for Office 365 to neutralize the already-delivered copies automatically. Which capability addresses this scenario?

communityTop.text: Zero-hour auto purge continuously reevaluates delivered cloud-mailbox messages as threat intelligence changes and can move or quarantine messages later identified as phishing, spam, or malware. Safe Attachments evaluates content during delivery, the Tenant Allow/Block List sets explicit allow or block entries, and message trace investigates mail flow. Those features do not provide this automated post-delivery cleanup behavior.

text: A hunter wants to query Microsoft Defender for Office 365 telemetry for sender addresses, recipients, filtering verdicts, and the final delivery action taken on messages. Which Advanced Hunting table is the most appropriate starting point?

communityTop.text: EmailEvents contains Defender for Office 365 message-processing telemetry, including sender and recipient information, threat verdict fields, and the email action or delivery information needed for this hunt. DeviceNetworkEvents is endpoint network telemetry, IdentityInfo describes identity context, and AlertEvidence lists entities associated with alerts rather than the full email-processing records requested.

text:
A hunter wants one result set containing rows from 2 compatible telemetry tables and does not need to correlate matching keys between individual rows. What does the following KQL operator accomplish?

union EmailEvents, UrlClickEvents

choices.text: Returns rows from both input tables in one result set
Matches rows from both tables on a shared identifier
Aggregates both tables into one count per time bucket
Removes rows that do not exist identically in both tables

communityTop.text: The KQL union operator returns the rows from two or more input tables as one result set, with schema handling determined by the union kind. The join operator is the tempting alternative when rows must be matched on a key such as an identifier. summarize performs aggregation, and union does not require identical rows to exist in both sources.

text: A hunter has an account, an IP address, several cloud resources, and a device that may be connected to one campaign. The hunter wants to traverse and visualize the relationships among these entities rather than analyze each as an isolated table row. Which capability best fits?

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel Graph is designed to model, analyze, and visualize relationships among interconnected identities, assets, activities, and threat intelligence, which supports graph-based investigation and traversal. A data collection rule controls ingestion, email notifications report events, and eDiscovery exports content. None of those alternatives provides relationship-centric security graph analysis.

text: A security team wants an AI-enabled client to use a standardized interface for natural-language security tasks such as finding relevant Sentinel tables, retrieving data, analyzing entities, triaging incidents, and hunting for threats under the user's existing permissions. Which component is designed for this?

choices.text: Defender for Endpoint attack surface reduction rules

communityTop.text: The Microsoft Sentinel Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server exposes security-focused tool collections through a standardized interface so compatible AI clients can search tables, retrieve data, analyze entities, triage incidents, and support threat hunting. Workbooks visualize data, ASR rules block endpoint behaviors, and Purview lifecycle controls information retention rather than providing AI tool access to Sentinel security data.

text: An organization uses a non-Microsoft antivirus product as the primary antivirus solution, while Microsoft Defender Antivirus remains in passive mode. The SOC wants Defender for Endpoint to remediate malicious artifacts detected by post-breach EDR signals even when the primary antivirus misses them. Which advanced feature should be enabled?

choices.text: Endpoint detection and response in block mode
Tamper protection for endpoint security settings

communityTop.text: Endpoint detection and response (EDR) in block mode is designed for this exact situation: Microsoft Defender Antivirus can remain passive while Defender for Endpoint uses behavioral EDR detections to block and remediate malicious artifacts missed by the primary antivirus. Network protection and other controls depend on different enforcement paths. Tamper protection protects security settings from unauthorized changes, but it does not provide the requested post-breach remediation behavior.

text: A Defender for Endpoint tenant has the advanced feature Automatically resolve alerts enabled. An analyst manually changes one alert to In progress, and the associated automated investigation later reports that no threats were found. Why might the alert remain In progress instead of being auto-resolved?

choices.text: Manual analyst status prevents auto-resolution from overwriting that alert
Auto-resolution works only for alerts generated through Microsoft Sentinel analytics
No-threat verdicts require a separate Microsoft Purview approval
Auto-resolution changes device risk but never changes alert status

communityTop.text: The auto-resolve feature can resolve alerts when no threats are found or when detected threats are remediated, but it does not overwrite an alert that a security analyst has manually set to In progress or Resolved. The feature is part of Defender for Endpoint and is not limited to Sentinel-created alerts. Purview approval is unrelated, and the feature can change alert status as well as indirectly affect device risk through the active-alert set.

text: A Sentinel automation rule is configured to run an incident-triggered playbook, but the playbook is unavailable because Sentinel itself lacks permission on the playbook resource group. Which Azure role should be granted to the Microsoft Sentinel service account on that resource group?

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor is the role that allows the Sentinel service account to run playbooks from automation rules and incident workflows in the resource group. Sentinel Responder is an analyst-facing role for incident work, while Reader roles permit viewing rather than execution. The permission must exist for the Sentinel service account in addition to the human operator having the roles needed for the workflow.

text: A custom network appliance sends verbose JSON records to Microsoft Sentinel. Before the records are stored, the SOC wants to drop low-value rows and mask a sensitive identifier while preserving the useful fields for later detections. Which mechanism is designed for this?

choices.text: A data collection rule transformation applied during ingestion
A workbook parameter applied when the dashboard loads
An incident automation rule applied after an alert fires
A scheduled analytics rule that deletes matching records after they are stored

communityTop.text: Data collection rule transformations use KQL on incoming data before it is stored, allowing the pipeline to filter rows, reshape fields, enrich records, or mask sensitive values. A workbook only changes how stored data is queried and displayed. Automation rules operate on incidents and alerts, and analytics rules detect patterns in stored telemetry rather than serving as an ingestion-time data-cleaning mechanism.

text: Threat indicators from several feeds are already present in Microsoft Sentinel, and firewall events are flowing from connected data sources. The SOC wants Sentinel to generate incidents when those indicators match observed network activity. Which detection approach most directly fits the requirement?

choices.text: Enable an appropriate TI map analytics rule
Create a workbook that lists active indicators
Assign a Sentinel incident responder role
Run an endpoint investigation package collection

communityTop.text: Threat-intelligence map analytics rules compare imported indicators with events arriving from connected data sources and generate security alerts and incidents when matches occur. A workbook can visualize indicators but does not create detections. RBAC affects permissions, and an endpoint investigation package gathers host artifacts rather than correlating threat indicators with network telemetry.

text: A team has onboarded Microsoft Sentinel to the Microsoft Defender portal and cannot enable the older Fusion Advanced multistage attack detection analytics rule. What best explains this behavior in the current unified experience?

choices.text: Microsoft Defender XDR correlation replaces Fusion for onboarded workspaces
Fusion requires all telemetry to be stored only in the Data Lake tier
Fusion can run only when all contributing alerts originate from scheduled analytics rules
Fusion was replaced by Microsoft Purview Audit for multi-stage attacks

communityTop.text: For Sentinel workspaces onboarded to the Microsoft Defender portal, the older Fusion rule is disabled because Microsoft Defender XDR provides the cross-product incident correlation function in the unified experience. Data tier selection is not the reason, and Fusion never required every signal to come from scheduled rules. Microsoft Purview Audit is an investigation data source, not the replacement correlation engine.

text: A security engineer wants Defender for Endpoint file-hash indicators to block a harmful portable executable on supported Windows endpoints. Which TWO prerequisites are specifically required for the Allow or block file feature?

choices.text: Microsoft Defender Antivirus is the active antimalware solution
Microsoft Defender Antivirus is permanently disabled
All endpoints are isolated from the network first
Microsoft Sentinel is configured as the primary SIEM platform for the organization

communityTop.text: The Allow or block file capability requires Microsoft Defender Antivirus to be the active antimalware solution and cloud-delivered protection to be enabled. Those components provide the enforcement and cloud intelligence path used by the file indicator. Device isolation and Microsoft Sentinel are separate controls, while disabling Defender Antivirus removes a prerequisite rather than satisfying one.

text: Three Sentinel automation rules can all match the same newly created incident. The SOC requires a tagging rule to run before an assignment rule, and both must run before a playbook is called. Which automation-rule setting controls that sequence?

communityTop.text: The Order value determines the sequence in which matching Microsoft Sentinel automation rules execute, which is important when later actions depend on changes made by earlier rules. Expiration controls how long a rule remains active, while an analytics template defines detection logic rather than automation sequencing. Incident severity can be used as a condition but does not itself determine execution order.

text: An external assessor must review Microsoft Sentinel data and configuration but should not change incidents, create analytics rules, or modify content. Which built-in Sentinel role best matches this least-privilege requirement?

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel Reader provides read access to Sentinel data and resources without the incident-management and content-authoring permissions granted by higher roles. Responder is intended for working incidents, and Contributor can create and modify Sentinel resources. Automation Contributor is narrowly intended to let Sentinel run playbooks and is not an analyst viewing role.

text: A data loss prevention policy flags a user for sending regulated data to an external destination. The analyst needs to investigate the DLP alert together with related security context, while the compliance engineer separately maintains the policy definition. Where should the analyst primarily investigate the alert?

choices.text: The Microsoft Purview policy creation page
The Microsoft Entra application registrations page
The Defender for Endpoint device inventory

communityTop.text: Microsoft recommends the Microsoft Defender XDR dashboard for investigating and managing DLP alerts because it brings the alert into the broader security investigation experience. The Microsoft Purview portal remains the recommended place to create and edit DLP policies, which is a different task. Entra app registration and endpoint inventory do not provide the DLP investigation workflow described.

text: Investigation confirms that a user-consented OAuth application is malicious and should no longer access organizational cloud data. Which Defender for Cloud Apps action most directly removes the application's granted access?

choices.text: Ban or revoke the OAuth application
Dismiss the activity alert as benign
Add the application to a Sentinel workbook

communityTop.text: Defender for Cloud Apps provides OAuth application remediation actions that can ban or revoke a risky application, removing the permissions that gave it access to cloud data. Dismissing an alert leaves the application access unchanged. A workbook is only a visualization surface, and an endpoint investigation package collects host evidence rather than changing OAuth consent or enterprise-application access.

text: A malicious executable is currently running on several known endpoints. The SOC needs to terminate it and quarantine the file on those devices immediately, then plans to create a longer-lived block afterward. Which Defender for Endpoint response action should be used first?

communityTop.text: Stop and quarantine file is the targeted response action that attempts to stop the malicious file and quarantine it on affected devices. Microsoft recommends a file indicator when the organization needs the file to remain blocked beyond the response-action delivery window. Restrict app execution locks the device to Microsoft-signed code more broadly, while package collection and scanning serve investigation or malware discovery rather than this precise file action.

text: An analyst finishes a Defender XDR investigation and resolves the incident. The SOC wants the record to show both whether the incident was a true or false positive and, for a true positive, what kind of threat it represented. Which incident properties capture those two judgments?

choices.text: Severity and the assigned incident owner

communityTop.text: Classification records the analyst judgment such as True positive or False positive, while determination records the threat category for a resolved incident. Severity expresses potential impact and ownership identifies responsibility, but neither records those analytical conclusions. Status, tags, device risk, and detection source provide workflow or context rather than the requested resolution judgments.

text: A junior responder opens a complex incident and needs contextual recommendations for triage, containment, further investigation, and remediation. The analyst wants suggested actions that can be reviewed before being applied rather than an opaque automatic response. Which embedded capability best fits?

communityTop.text: Security Copilot guided responses generate contextual response cards for triage, containment, investigation, and remediation, explaining what action is recommended and why so an analyst can review it before acting. Summary rules aggregate telemetry, notification rules send messages, and retention policies govern information lifecycle. None of those alternatives provides interactive incident-response recommendations.

text: A Defender for Cloud Apps activity alert shows a user repeatedly accessing cloud resources from a risky source, and the SOC wants to contain the account while it determines whether the behavior is malicious. Which response is designed for this immediate identity containment?

choices.text: Suspend the user account from the investigation workflow
Delete the Sentinel workspace containing the alert
Disable endpoint network protection across the tenant
Convert the activity alert into a Purview retention label

communityTop.text: Defender for Cloud Apps investigation workflows support suspending a user when suspicious cloud activity warrants immediate containment while the SOC determines the appropriate remediation. Deleting the workspace destroys security visibility, disabling network protection weakens endpoint controls, and a retention label manages information lifecycle. None of those alternatives directly contains the risky user identity.

text: A workstation is compromised and the responder wants to prevent most untrusted programs from launching while keeping the device available for further investigation. Which Defender for Endpoint action applies a code integrity policy that permits only Microsoft-signed files to run?

communityTop.text: Restrict app execution applies a code integrity policy that allows only files signed by a Microsoft-issued certificate to run, helping prevent an attacker from launching additional untrusted programs on the compromised device. Investigation packages collect evidence, antivirus scans search for malware, and device tags organize assets. Those alternatives do not impose the requested execution lockdown.

text: A hunter needs endpoint telemetry showing outbound connections, including RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol, and the initiating process. Which Microsoft Defender XDR Advanced Hunting table is the best starting point?

communityTop.text: DeviceNetworkEvents contains network connection and related endpoint events, including remote addresses, ports, URLs, protocols, and initiating-process fields. DeviceNetworkInfo describes adapter and network configuration rather than connection events. DeviceProcessEvents focuses on process creation, while EmailUrlInfo describes URLs found in email telemetry rather than endpoint network sessions.

text:
A hunter has many records per device and wants the complete most recent row for each DeviceId, not merely the latest timestamp value. Which KQL pattern best meets the requirement?

DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId

choices.text: Returns the full row with the greatest Timestamp for each DeviceId
Returns only the largest Timestamp value across the entire table
Joins each DeviceId to every row having a different timestamp
Counts how many rows each DeviceId produced during the query window

communityTop.text: The summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId pattern returns, for each device group, the row where Timestamp is greatest and includes all columns because the wildcard is requested. A plain max() would return only the maximum value rather than the associated row. join correlates rows between inputs, and count would aggregate volume instead of selecting the latest record.

text: During a Sentinel hunt, an analyst finds a suspicious query result that may become evidence in a later incident. Which THREE items are preserved with a hunting bookmark so the analyst can revisit the finding in context?

communityTop.text: A Sentinel hunting bookmark preserves the selected result information together with the source KQL query and the time range that produced it, allowing the hunter to return to the finding and continue investigation in context. Licensing assignment and pricing-tier history are administrative properties unrelated to the bookmarked hunt result. Bookmarks can also be enriched with entities, tags, MITRE mappings, and notes.

text: A hunter is building a long KQL query and wants to define a suspicious-IP list once, give that expression a name, and reuse the name in several later parts of the query. Which KQL construct is intended for this?

communityTop.text: A KQL let statement binds a name to a scalar expression, tabular expression, function, or view so the query can be decomposed into reusable named parts. project selects or reshapes columns, distinct removes duplicate combinations, and render controls visualization. Those operators do not define a reusable named expression for later references in the same query.

text: A responder can run signed PowerShell scripts during a Defender for Endpoint live response session, but an internally written unsigned script is rejected. Which tenant setting most directly enables that script to run?

choices.text: Allow unsigned script execution in live response
Share endpoint alerts with Microsoft Purview

communityTop.text: Defender for Endpoint has a specific advanced feature that permits unsigned PowerShell scripts in live response sessions. Live response itself can already be enabled while unsigned scripts remain blocked, so the additional unsigned-script setting is what changes this behavior. Endpoint notifications, authenticated telemetry, and Purview alert sharing serve different purposes and do not relax script-signature enforcement.

text: An insider-risk team wants endpoint security alerts and their triage status to contribute context to Microsoft Purview insider risk investigations. Which Defender for Endpoint advanced feature provides this integration?

choices.text: Share endpoint alerts with Microsoft Compliance Center
Restrict correlation to scoped device groups

communityTop.text: The endpoint alert sharing advanced feature sends Defender for Endpoint security alerts and their triage status to Microsoft Purview so insider risk workflows can use that context. Web content filtering controls browsing categories, scoped correlation changes how endpoint alerts are correlated, and streamlined connectivity affects device onboarding communications. None of those alternatives sends endpoint alert context into Purview.

text: A company wants Microsoft Intune compliance and Conditional Access decisions to use device risk calculated by Defender for Endpoint. The Defender portal connection is enabled, but no risk information reaches Intune. What configuration should the engineer verify next?

choices.text: The Defender for Endpoint integration is also enabled in Microsoft Intune
Every Sentinel analytics rule maps a Device entity
A Defender live response session is active on each managed device
The devices are assigned to the highest Defender automation level

communityTop.text: The Defender for Endpoint and Intune integration must be enabled on both sides before Defender device risk can participate in Intune and Conditional Access workflows. Entity mapping affects Sentinel investigations, while live response and automation levels control endpoint response operations. Neither substitutes for enabling the actual Intune integration in the Intune administration experience.

text: A Sentinel administrator searches the Data connectors page for a supported third-party product, but the connector is not listed even though Microsoft documents it as available through Sentinel. What should the administrator check first?

choices.text: Install the solution that provides the connector from Content hub
Whether all existing incidents have been resolved
Whether the workspace has at least one custom workbook
Whether threat intelligence indicators have been imported

communityTop.text: Many Microsoft Sentinel data connectors are delivered as part of solutions in Content hub. If the relevant solution has not been installed, its connector might not appear on the Data connectors page for configuration. Incident status, workbook presence, and threat-indicator ingestion do not control whether a packaged connector is made available to the workspace.

text: A large enterprise frequently adds and removes Windows workstations. Security events from those workstations must be forwarded to central Windows Event Collectors without administrators maintaining an explicit source-computer list in each subscription. Which WEF subscription model best fits?

communityTop.text: A source-initiated Windows Event Forwarding subscription defines the subscription on the collector while source computers are configured, commonly through Group Policy, to forward events to it. This works well when the collector should not maintain a fixed list of every source computer. Collector-initiated subscriptions require the event sources to be specified when the subscription is created; the other choices are not WEF subscription types.

text: A team creates a new destination table for the Microsoft Sentinel Custom Logs via AMA connector to ingest a text application log directly from the host. Which TWO requirements apply to the initial custom table?

choices.text: The table includes a TimeGenerated datetime field
The table includes an AlertId GUID field
The table must use the CommonSecurityLog schema

communityTop.text: For a new Custom Logs via AMA destination table, Microsoft requires a custom-table name ending in _CL and a TimeGenerated column of type datetime. The connector also uses a string field for the log message, such as RawData when collecting directly from the host. SecurityEvent and CommonSecurityLog are different schemas, and AlertId is not a mandatory field for this custom text-log table.

text: A Defender XDR custom detection query joins DeviceProcessEvents to DeviceNetworkEvents. The author wants to select Continuous (NRT) frequency, but the rule is not eligible. Which query characteristic explains the restriction?

choices.text: Continuous custom detections must reference only one table
Continuous rules cannot include any time filter
Continuous rules require a Microsoft Sentinel workbook
Continuous rules can use only email-related tables

communityTop.text: Continuous near-real-time custom detections are eligible only when the query references one table and uses supported KQL features. A query that joins DeviceProcessEvents and DeviceNetworkEvents therefore fails the one-table requirement even if the logic is otherwise valid. Time filters, workbooks, and email-only schemas are not the defining eligibility rule in this scenario.

text: An analyst opens a Sentinel scheduled analytics rule template from an installed solution. The template lists a required data source that is not connected, and the Create rule action is unavailable. What is the most appropriate next step?

choices.text: Enable the required data source before creating the rule
Convert the template into a hunting bookmark
Assign every incident to the analyst
Move the workspace to the Data lake tier

communityTop.text: Sentinel analytics rule templates declare the data sources their query logic depends on, and Sentinel checks those sources when the template is opened. If a required source is unavailable, the rule cannot produce meaningful results and the creation action can be disabled. Bookmarks, incident ownership, and storage-tier changes do not satisfy the template's missing telemetry dependency.

text: An analyst confirms that a Microsoft Entra risky user is genuinely compromised and selects Confirm user compromised. What does that action do to the risk record?

choices.text: Sets user risk to high and adds an admin-confirmed compromise detection
Immediately resets the password and closes every associated incident
Marks the user safe and removes the detections from future learning
Deletes the risky sign-ins while leaving the user risk unchanged

communityTop.text: Confirm user compromised records the analyst's true-positive judgment: Microsoft Entra ID Protection sets the user risk to high and adds an Admin confirmed user compromised detection. The user remains risky until remediation actions are completed. Password reset and session revocation can be appropriate follow-up containment steps, but they are not automatically performed merely by recording the compromise judgment.

text: A sanctioned penetration test generates a real Microsoft Entra risk detection for a test account. The detection is valid, but the activity is known and nonmalicious. Which risk disposition best matches that finding?

communityTop.text: Microsoft describes Dismiss user risk as appropriate for a benign positive: the detected risky behavior is real, but it is not malicious, such as activity from a known penetration test. Confirm user safe is used for a false positive and teaches the system that similar activity should not be treated as risky. Confirm compromised records a true compromise, while blocking the user is a containment action rather than the correct disposition for an approved test.

text: A responder removes a confirmed phishing message from users' mailboxes with the Soft delete action in Threat Explorer. Where is the message moved so that it can still be recoverable subject to mailbox retention?

communityTop.text: Soft delete moves the message into the mailbox Recoverable Items Deletions folder, which preserves the possibility of recovery according to the mailbox retention configuration. Moving to Junk is a separate remediation choice, while permanent purge behavior is associated with hard deletion and retention processing. Sentinel incident records track investigations and do not store the remediated email message.

text: While reviewing a Defender XDR incident attack story, an analyst identifies a suspicious device and wants to investigate its broader activity without manually rebuilding a query from scratch. Which incident action is designed to pivot directly into relevant Advanced Hunting queries for that entity?

communityTop.text: The Go hunt action pivots from an entity in the incident experience into Advanced Hunting and offers relevant queries for that entity, such as all activity or related alerts. Collecting an investigation package gathers endpoint artifacts but does not perform the cross-table hunting pivot. Workbooks visualize data, and incident severity changes case metadata rather than expanding the investigation.

text: An incident contains an obfuscated PowerShell event in the attack story. The responder wants an AI-assisted explanation of the script and a mapping of behaviors in the script to ATT&CK techniques. Which embedded capability should be used?

communityTop.text: Security Copilot script analysis in the Defender incident and device-timeline experiences can explain suspicious scripts or command lines and surface associated MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Workbook parameters change visualization inputs, device discovery finds unmanaged assets, and Purview Content search locates Microsoft 365 content. None of those alternatives performs AI-assisted script interpretation.

text: A Defender for Cloud Apps alert points to an unusual cloud activity. The analyst wants to inspect exactly what event data the connected application sent rather than relying only on the normalized activity view. Which option in the activity drawer provides that evidence?

communityTop.text: The Defender for Cloud Apps activity drawer includes View raw data, which exposes the event information received from the connected application and can help validate how the normalized activity was derived. Tags organize items, an investigation package is an endpoint collection action, and Sentinel summary rules aggregate log data. Those features do not reveal the original app-provided activity record.

text: A rogue network device cannot run Defender for Endpoint, but it is communicating with several Defender-onboarded endpoints. The SOC wants those onboarded endpoints to block communications with the rogue device while investigation continues. Which response action best matches this objective?

communityTop.text: Contain device is intended to make Defender for Endpoint onboarded devices block communication with the contained device, including updating the block if that device's IP changes. Isolation is different: it restricts the network connectivity of an onboarded endpoint itself. App restriction limits executable trust on an endpoint, and an investigation package collects evidence without enforcing network containment.

text: A hunter needs both alert severity and the files, IP addresses, users, or devices associated with each alert. Which TWO Advanced Hunting tables should be correlated on AlertId?

communityTop.text: AlertInfo contains alert-level metadata such as title, category, severity, service source, and attack techniques. AlertEvidence contains the files, IP addresses, URLs, users, devices, and other entities associated with those alerts, and Microsoft documents joining the two on AlertId. DeviceInfo, EmailEvents, and IdentityInfo can enrich other hunts, but they are not the paired alert-metadata and alert-evidence tables requested.

text: A hunter is looking for a malicious executable that might have been created, renamed, or modified on Windows endpoints. Which Advanced Hunting table is the best starting point for those file-system events?

communityTop.text: DeviceFileEvents contains file creation, modification, and other file-system events generated from Defender for Endpoint telemetry. DeviceNetworkEvents focuses on network connections, EmailEvents covers mail processing and delivery, and IdentityLogonEvents covers authentication activity. Those tables may help correlate an investigation later, but they are not the primary source for endpoint file-system changes.

text: Persistence is suspected through modification of Windows registry run keys on several endpoints. Which Advanced Hunting table should a hunter query first for registry-entry creation and modification events?

communityTop.text: DeviceRegistryEvents is the Advanced Hunting table dedicated to creation and modification of Windows registry entries, making it the direct source for investigating run-key persistence. DeviceProcessEvents records process creation, AlertInfo contains alert metadata, and EmailUrlInfo describes URLs in email. Those sources can provide surrounding context but do not directly represent registry-entry changes.

text: A hunter wants a case-insensitive match for the whole indexed term powershell within a command-line column, rather than matching the same characters inside a larger word. Which KQL operator is the better fit?

communityTop.text: The KQL has operator performs a case-insensitive search for a whole term and can use the term index for terms of 3 or more characters. contains searches for a character subsequence and can therefore match text inside larger terms, while also generally being less efficient for a term search. startswith constrains the position, and a regular expression is unnecessary for this straightforward indexed-term match.

text: A complex Advanced Hunting query parses a large JSON column and then applies a one-hour time filter. The query repeatedly approaches resource limits. Which change best follows Microsoft's query optimization guidance?

choices.text: Apply the time filter before parsing the JSON
Replace the time filter with an unscoped search
Parse every column before reducing the result set
Expand the query to union all available schema tables
