communityTop.text: Microsoft recommends applying time and other selective filters early so fewer records reach expensive transformation and parsing operations such as parse_json. Moving the one-hour filter ahead of parsing reduces the amount of data that the parser must process. Unscoped search and broad union operations increase work, and parsing more columns before filtering moves the query in the opposite direction from the recommended optimization pattern.

text: A SOC wants email messages only when High-severity endpoint alerts affect devices in the production-server device group. Which configuration most directly provides that filtering?

choices.text: An alert email rule scoped to the production-server group and High severity
A Sentinel automation rule that assigns every incident to the server team
A Sentinel workbook filtered to the production-server device group
A Defender XDR Threat analytics notification rule filtered by report tags

communityTop.text: Defender XDR alert email notification rules can scope notifications to selected device groups and alert severity levels, which directly matches the requirement. A Sentinel automation rule changes incident handling rather than the Defender alert-email subscription. Workbooks visualize data, and Threat analytics notifications track report publications or updates instead of endpoint alert severity.

text: An analyst wants email only when Microsoft publishes or updates Threat analytics reports tagged for ransomware, rather than notifications for every new security alert. What should be configured?

choices.text: An incident notification rule filtered to High severity
A Threat analytics notification rule filtered by report tag
An endpoint alert notification rule scoped to a device group
A Sentinel scheduled analytics rule that emails the analyst

communityTop.text: Threat analytics has its own email notification rules, and those rules can target all report updates or only reports matching selected types or tags. Incident and endpoint alert notification rules are driven by security detections, not by publication of research reports. A Sentinel scheduled analytics rule queries workspace data and is not the subscription mechanism for Threat analytics report updates.

text: A Defender for Endpoint device group uses Full - remediate threats automatically. Automated investigation determines that a file is malicious. What should an analyst expect?

choices.text: The remediation action waits for approval on the Action center Pending tab
Automatic remediation, with the result recorded in Action center History
The investigation records a verdict but never performs a remediation action
The device is automatically deleted from its Defender device group

communityTop.text: With full automation, Defender for Endpoint performs remediation actions automatically on artifacts determined to be malicious. Completed remediation actions are tracked on the Action center History tab and can be reviewed, and supported actions can be undone if necessary. Pending approval is characteristic of semi-automation, while device-group membership is not removed as part of remediation.

text: A device group is configured as Semi - require approval for all folders. Automated investigation proposes remediation of a malicious file, but no analyst approves or rejects the action. What happens to the pending action?

choices.text: It is approved automatically after 24 hours
It times out after 7 days, which is treated as a rejection
It remains pending until the device is removed from the group
It is promoted to full automation after the next investigation

communityTop.text: Under the semi-automation level that requires approval for all folders, file remediation actions wait in the Action center Pending tab. Microsoft documents that pending actions time out after 7 days, and a timed-out action behaves the same as a rejected action. The timeout does not change the device-group automation level or automatically authorize the remediation.

text: A workstation matches the membership rules for two Defender for Endpoint device groups. One group has rank 1 and the other has rank 3. Which group receives the device?

choices.text: Both groups, because matching groups are cumulative
The rank 3 group, because higher numbers have greater priority
The rank 1 group, because rank 1 has highest priority
Neither group until an administrator resolves the overlap manually

communityTop.text: Defender for Endpoint resolves overlapping device-group rules by rank. Rank 1 is the highest priority, and when a device matches more than one group it is added only to the highest-ranked matching group. Membership is therefore not cumulative, and administrators do not need to resolve each overlap manually before a device can be grouped.

text: An organization enables Defender for Endpoint role-based access control. A user previously relied only on the Microsoft Entra Security Reader role for read-only portal access. What should the security administrator plan for?

choices.text: The user keeps identical access because Entra read-only roles bypass Defender RBAC
The user loses portal access until assigned through Defender RBAC
The user automatically receives the Defender for Endpoint Global Administrator role
The user can view all devices but loses only the ability to export reports

communityTop.text: After Defender for Endpoint RBAC is enabled, users who previously had read-only access through roles such as Microsoft Entra Security Reader lose that access until they are assigned through the Defender RBAC model. Administrator roles have different behavior, but read-only users are not automatically promoted. Planning the RBAC role and group assignments before enabling the feature prevents accidental lockout.

text: A team is piloting an attack surface reduction rule before broad enforcement and is also testing a user-facing temporary exception workflow. Which TWO statements about ASR rule modes are correct?

choices.text: Audit mode evaluates detections without blocking the matching activity
Warn mode can provide a temporary 24-hour bypass after approval
Audit mode permanently excludes the detected file from every ASR rule
Warn mode disables the rule until an administrator manually re-enables it
Block mode records events but intentionally allows the activity to continue

communityTop.text: Audit mode evaluates the ASR rule and records detections without enforcing a block, which is useful for measuring impact before deployment. Warn mode behaves like Block but can allow a temporary bypass for 24 hours; current Defender behavior requires administrator approval for the Unblock action. Persistent exceptions should use an appropriate ASR exclusion, while Block mode actually prevents the targeted behavior.

text: A scheduled penetration test will create predictable Sentinel incidents for 3 days. The SOC wants a temporary automation rule to handle this known noise and then stop automatically. Which setting best supports that plan?

choices.text: Set an expiration date on the automation rule
Set the analytics rule lookback period to 3 days
Change the incident provider to Microsoft Defender XDR
Create a workbook parameter for the penetration-test dates

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel automation rules can have an expiration date, after which the rule is disabled. Microsoft specifically identifies time-limited activity such as penetration testing as a useful scenario for this capability. A query lookback changes what an analytics rule examines, while incident-provider filters and workbook parameters do not automatically retire an incident-handling automation rule.

text: A Sentinel automation rule uses the When alert is created trigger. The analyst opens Run playbook but the intended playbook is unavailable in the selection list. The playbook starts with an incident trigger. What is the most direct fix?

choices.text: Use an alert-triggered playbook so its trigger matches the rule
Increase the automation rule order so the playbook appears later
Convert the playbook to a Sentinel workbook before attaching it
Change the playbook resource group to the Sentinel workspace resource group

communityTop.text: An automation rule can run only playbooks whose trigger type matches the rule trigger. A rule triggered when an alert is created therefore offers alert-triggered playbooks, not incident-triggered ones. Rule order controls execution sequence, and resource-group permissions can gray out an otherwise compatible playbook, but neither changes an incident trigger into an alert trigger.

text: An analyst must open a Sentinel incident and manually run an existing playbook on that incident. Which TWO Azure roles directly cover those two capabilities?

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel Responder provides access to the incident so the analyst can work with it, while Microsoft Sentinel Playbook Operator allows the analyst to run a playbook manually. Automation Contributor is used by the Sentinel service account so automation rules can run playbooks automatically. Reader and Log Analytics Contributor do not together grant the requested manual incident-and-playbook capabilities.

text: A SOC finds a Microsoft Sentinel workbook template that is delivered by a Content hub solution but the template is not available in the workspace. What should be done before the team can use that template?

choices.text: Install the relevant solution or standalone workbook from Content hub
Create an NRT analytics rule with the same name as the workbook template
Move the workspace table plan from Analytics to Data Lake
Assign every SOC analyst the Global Administrator role

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel workbook templates are delivered through Content hub solutions and can also be installed as standalone workbook items. The content must be installed before the template is available for use in the workspace. Analytics-rule creation and table-tier changes do not install workbook content, and Global Administrator is unnecessary because workbook access should use the appropriate workbook permissions.

text: A high-volume table is moved from the Analytics tier to Data Lake-only storage to reduce real-time ingestion cost. Which consequence should the SOC expect for that table?

choices.text: Real-time Sentinel analytics on that table stop working
The table is deleted as soon as its Analytics retention period ends
The table can no longer be queried with KQL under any circumstances
All historical data is automatically promoted back to the Analytics tier each day

communityTop.text: Data Lake-only storage is intended for lower-cost long-term retention, but features that depend on Analytics-tier data, such as real-time alerting and interactive Sentinel analytics, are no longer available for that table. The data is not deleted merely because it leaves Analytics, and Data Lake data remains queryable through supported lake capabilities. Promotion back to Analytics is an explicit operation, not a daily automatic process.

text: A SOC optimization recommends reducing ingestion for a table. The team reviews the recommendation and decides not to implement it because the data is required by a regulatory control. Which optimization action best records that decision?

communityTop.text: Dismiss is the appropriate status when the SOC does not plan to take the recommended action and no longer wants the optimization to remain in the active list. Complete indicates that the recommended actions were carried out, while In progress signals active implementation. Triggering a new evaluation recalculates the recommendation and does not record the decision to reject it.

text: A company wants to reduce Windows Security event volume while retaining a threat-focused set of important events. A complete sign-in/sign-out audit trail is not required. Which Windows Security Events via AMA collection set best fits?

choices.text: Custom with every Security event ID selected

communityTop.text: The Minimal set is designed as a small collection of Windows Security events that can indicate potential threats, including important sign-in and process-creation activity, without preserving a complete audit trail. Common includes a fuller auditing set such as sign-out events, while All collects the complete supported Security and AppLocker event set. A custom rule selecting every event would defeat the volume-reduction goal.

text: An engineer creates a generic Azure Monitor Agent data collection rule for the Windows Security log and sends it to Log Analytics. Built-in Sentinel detections that query SecurityEvent return no data. Which change most directly aligns the collection with those detections?

choices.text: Use Windows Security Events via AMA so records land in SecurityEvent
Add a workbook that aliases Event to SecurityEvent at query time
Move the Event table to the Data Lake tier and wait for schema conversion
Enable a Threat Intelligence TAXII connector for the same workspace

communityTop.text: A generic Azure Monitor Windows Events data source sends the Security log to the Event table. The Microsoft Sentinel Windows Security Events via AMA connector uses the same Azure Monitor Agent but sends those security events to SecurityEvent, which is the table queried by many built-in Sentinel Windows detections. Workbooks, data-tier changes, and threat-intelligence connectors do not change the event destination schema.

text: A security engineer needs Azure resource platform logs available for Microsoft Sentinel queries in the workspace where Sentinel is enabled. Which diagnostic-setting destination should be selected?

choices.text: Send to a Log Analytics workspace
Archive only to an Azure Storage account
Stream only to an Event Hubs namespace
Send only to a partner solution outside Azure Monitor

communityTop.text: For Microsoft Sentinel to query Azure resource logs in its workspace, the diagnostic setting should send the selected logs to the relevant Log Analytics workspace. Storage is useful for archival and Event Hubs for streaming to downstream systems, but neither by itself places the records in the Sentinel workspace tables used for analytics. A partner destination likewise does not satisfy the stated workspace-query requirement.

text: A custom Sentinel detection written before 2026 still queries the legacy ThreatIntelligenceIndicator table and now misses newly ingested intelligence. Which table should the detection use for STIX indicator data in the current schema?

communityTop.text: Microsoft moved Sentinel threat-intelligence ingestion to the newer STIX-aligned ThreatIntelIndicators and ThreatIntelObjects tables and stopped ingesting new data into the legacy ThreatIntelligenceIndicator table after July 31, 2025. ThreatIntelIndicators is therefore the current table for STIX indicator records. SecurityAlert, CommonSecurityLog, and SentinelHealth contain different classes of security data.

text: An analyst configures a scheduled Sentinel analytics rule to run every 15 minutes but sets its query lookback period to only 5 minutes. Which adjustment follows the scheduled-rule timing requirement?

choices.text: Increase the query period to at least 15 minutes
Reduce the query period to 1 minute
Change the rule to an anomaly template without a query
Keep the values because query frequency can exceed query period

communityTop.text: For a scheduled analytics rule, queryFrequency must be less than or equal to queryPeriod. A rule that runs every 15 minutes therefore needs a lookback period of at least 15 minutes if those settings are retained. A 5-minute query period would leave gaps between executions. Changing rule type does not correct the invalid relationship between the scheduling frequency and the lookback period.

text: A scheduled Sentinel analytics rule returns a SeverityFromQuery column whose value varies with each result. The SOC wants each generated alert to use that result-specific severity instead of the static severity configured on the rule. Which feature should be used?

choices.text: Query suppression after a generated result

communityTop.text: Alert details override can use fields returned by the analytics query to replace default alert properties, including severity, tactics, name, and description, on individual alert instances. Entity mapping promotes fields into entities for investigation, while incident grouping controls how alerts are aggregated. Query suppression pauses further rule execution after a result and does not dynamically set alert severity.

text: A new Sentinel workspace has customizable anomaly templates available. An analyst wants to inspect anomalies produced by the built-in templates before changing any thresholds. Which statement best describes the default behavior?

choices.text: They are active by default and write queryable results to the Anomalies table
Anomaly rules remain disabled until a custom machine-learning model is uploaded
Anomalies are written only to SecurityAlert and cannot be queried directly
Each anomaly template requires a playbook before it can generate a result

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel customizable anomaly rules are activated by default and can generate anomalies out of the box; those results are available for querying in the Anomalies table. Analysts can later tune thresholds and parameters through the analytics-rule interface. A custom model or playbook is not required for the built-in templates to start producing anomaly records.

text: A SOC has a large incident queue and needs to decide which case deserves attention first. An analyst opens the incident summary pane before entering the full investigation. Which information is specifically intended to support that prioritization decision?

choices.text: The incident priority assessment and the factors influencing its priority score
The raw KQL text from every analytics rule that contributed an alert
The complete device timeline for every endpoint represented in the incident
The retention policy for each data source that supplied incident evidence

communityTop.text: The Defender incident summary pane exposes a priority assessment together with the factors influencing that priority score so analysts can quickly judge relative urgency. KQL rule text, complete endpoint timelines, and source-retention settings can matter later in an investigation, but they are not the summary-pane elements Microsoft provides specifically for incident prioritization.

text: An analyst is tracing a multistage attack in the Defender XDR attack story and confirms that one displayed device must be isolated immediately. What is the main workflow advantage of taking the response action from the attack story?

choices.text: It lets the analyst remediate an entity while keeping the attack context visible
It converts every related alert into a separate Microsoft Sentinel incident
It permanently suppresses future alerts involving the same device and user
It exports the entire incident automatically to a Purview eDiscovery review set

communityTop.text: The attack story is designed to keep the connected entities and progression of the attack in view while the analyst investigates and responds. Supported remediation actions, such as isolating a device or deleting a file, can be initiated without leaving that context. The attack story does not split the incident, suppress future detections, or create an eDiscovery review set.

text: A Defender for Cloud incident has a documented containment workflow implemented as an Azure Logic App. The analyst wants to launch that workflow directly while responding to the incident. Which Take action option should be used?

communityTop.text: Defender for Cloud exposes Trigger automated response in the incident Take action experience specifically to launch a configured Logic App. Mitigate the threat presents manual remediation guidance, while Prevent future attacks surfaces security recommendations. Suppress similar alerts is for reducing future alert noise when the detection is not relevant, not for executing a containment workflow.

text: After investigating a Defender for Cloud incident, the team concludes that the activity is expected in this environment but also wants guidance that reduces exposure to this attack pattern. Which TWO Take action capabilities address those goals?

choices.text: Suppress similar alerts for future detections with the same characteristics
Review security recommendations under Prevent future attacks
Collect a Defender for Endpoint investigation package from every Azure resource
Create a Purview eDiscovery hold for the subscription
Move all correlated alerts to the MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs table

communityTop.text: When activity is legitimate or otherwise not relevant, Defender for Cloud can create a suppression rule for future alerts with similar characteristics. The Prevent future attacks section supplies security recommendations intended to improve posture against the same class of attack. Investigation packages, eDiscovery holds, and Microsoft Graph log tables serve different products and do not satisfy these two incident-response goals.

text: A user triggers a sign-in risk level covered by a risk-based Conditional Access policy. The activity is legitimate, and the user successfully completes the required multifactor authentication challenge. What should happen to that sign-in risk?

choices.text: It is remediated after the successful multifactor authentication
It stays at risk until an administrator resets the user's password
It becomes confirmed compromised because MFA was required
It is converted into a Microsoft Defender for Identity alert

communityTop.text: Microsoft Entra ID Protection can let users self-remediate sign-in risk through a risk-based Conditional Access policy. When the user successfully completes the required MFA challenge, the sign-in risk state is updated to Remediated. A password change is associated with user-risk remediation, not this sign-in-risk flow, and the event is not automatically converted into a Defender for Identity alert.

text: A password-based user is subject to a Conditional Access user-risk policy that requires risk remediation. The user knows the current password and is already registered for MFA. Which sequence remediates the user risk through the policy?

choices.text: Complete MFA, then perform a secure password change
Perform self-service password reset without first authenticating
Dismiss the user risk, then continue using the existing password
Approve the risky sign-in from the Defender XDR Action center

communityTop.text: For a password-based user, the Require risk remediation flow requires strong authentication and then a secure password change. Microsoft distinguishes this from self-service password reset: the user knows the current password, completes MFA, and changes it. Dismissing risk is an administrative disposition for a benign result, and the Defender Action center does not approve Entra user-risk remediation.

text: A company uses Defender for Identity sensors on domain controllers and wants analysts to disable compromised on-premises Active Directory users from Defender. Why should the managed action account be separate from the Directory Service account?

choices.text: It needs write permissions for remediation; the Directory Service account is read-only
The Directory Service account can change passwords but cannot read identity information
The managed action account is used only to query Microsoft Graph activity logs
The Directory Service account must be a Global Administrator in Microsoft Entra ID

communityTop.text: Defender for Identity separates identity-data collection from remediation. The Directory Service account is intended for reading Active Directory data, whereas managed response actions such as disabling an account or forcing a password reset require write permissions through the action account. Reusing the same credential unnecessarily expands privilege and increases the impact if that account is exposed.

text: An email security analyst reviews a message in Threat Explorer and confirms that Microsoft incorrectly classified the message as malicious. The analyst wants to provide that verdict back to Microsoft from the investigation workflow. Which action fits?

choices.text: Submit the message to Microsoft as confirmed clean
Hard delete the message from every recipient mailbox
Create an alert suppression rule for all messages from the sender
Move the message to the Recoverable Items folder

communityTop.text: Threat Explorer and the Email entity page let analysts use Take action to submit a message to Microsoft and explicitly report that it has been confirmed clean. That feedback path addresses a false positive. Hard deletion and other mailbox remediation actions remove content rather than correct the verdict, while broad sender suppression could hide future genuinely malicious mail.

text: An administrator submits a manual email remediation from Threat Explorer and the action is approved. Where should another responder go to track the remediation status and review its approval ID and history?

choices.text: The Microsoft Defender XDR Action center History tab
The Microsoft Entra risky users report
The Purview eDiscovery review set statistics page

communityTop.text: Approved manual email remediation actions are tracked centrally in the Microsoft Defender XDR Action center, including the History view and identifiers such as the approval ID. This provides a record of the action, source, status, and related investigation information. Sentinel anomalies, Entra risk reports, and eDiscovery review statistics do not track Defender for Office 365 remediation execution.

text: A Sentinel responder finishes an investigation and changes the incident status to Closed. Which additional item is required as part of closing the incident?

choices.text: A new analytics rule for the incident

communityTop.text: When a Microsoft Sentinel incident is closed, the responder must select a classification reason, such as true positive, benign positive, false positive, or undetermined. This records the disposition of the case and supports later metrics and tuning. Creating a new detection rule, identifying a Graph application, or collecting an endpoint package may be useful in some investigations but is not required simply to close the incident.

text: An endpoint alert shows that a suspicious PowerShell process started shortly after a document viewer launched. The analyst wants to inspect the parent-child process relationship around that event. Which device-timeline capability is most useful?

choices.text: Open the event's process tree view
Create a Defender for Cloud suppression rule

communityTop.text: The Defender for Endpoint device timeline can expose a process tree for an event, making parent-child process relationships visible during investigation. That is the direct way to determine whether the document viewer spawned the suspicious PowerShell process. Incident classifications, eDiscovery searches, and Defender for Cloud suppression rules operate on different evidence or workflows and do not reconstruct the endpoint process chain.

text: During a long endpoint investigation, an analyst marks several timeline events for follow-up and later wants the timeline to show only those marked events. What should the analyst do?

choices.text: Enable the Flagged events timeline filter
Change the incident severity to High
Move the device into a new device group
Run a full antivirus scan from Action center

communityTop.text: The device timeline supports flagging noteworthy events and then filtering the timeline to display only Flagged events. That lets the analyst return to a small set of evidence without changing the underlying event data. Incident severity, device-group membership, and antivirus scans affect prioritization or response, but they do not filter the timeline to the events the analyst previously marked.

text: A responder is in a Defender for Endpoint Live Response session and confirms that a malicious scheduled task provides persistence. Which Live Response command family is intended to remove a confirmed malicious entity such as a scheduled task?

communityTop.text: The Live Response remediate command is designed to remove or neutralize supported malicious entities; for a scheduled task, the remediation action removes the task. The putfile command transfers a library file to the device, library lists uploaded files, and collect obtains forensic material on supported platforms. Those commands support investigation or tooling but do not perform the entity remediation requested here.

text: An incident responder uploads a trusted diagnostic utility to the Live Response library and needs to place that utility onto an affected device for the current session. Which command is designed for this transfer?

communityTop.text: The Live Response putfile command copies a file from the Live Response library to the target device's working folder. Microsoft notes that these transferred files are deleted when the device restarts by default, making the feature suitable for temporary response tooling. Analyze evaluates an entity, release reverses isolation on supported platforms, and undo reverses supported remediation rather than transferring a file.

text: A responder downloads a Defender for Endpoint investigation package and wants evidence of persistence configured through known Windows auto-start entry points. Which package folder is most directly relevant?

communityTop.text: For Windows devices, the investigation package includes an Autoruns folder representing registry content from known auto-start entry points, which is directly useful for examining persistence. Network, prefetch, or browser artifacts can contribute other investigative context, but the documented Autoruns collection is the package component specifically aimed at identifying configured automatic-start locations.

text: An analyst realizes that a completed Defender response action should be reversed. The action type supports reversal. Where should the analyst review the completed action and initiate the undo operation?

communityTop.text: The Microsoft Defender XDR Action center tracks completed and pending response actions in one place, and supported completed actions can be undone from their action details. This gives responders an auditable way to reverse actions such as isolation or code restriction when appropriate. Content hub, Entra risk reports, and eDiscovery search statistics do not manage Defender response-action rollback.

text: A compromised endpoint uses a third-party antivirus product, so Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. The responder wants to use the Defender for Endpoint device action to scan the host for malware. What should the responder expect?

choices.text: A Defender Antivirus scan can still be started on the device
The scan action is unavailable whenever Defender Antivirus is passive
The device must first be removed from Defender for Endpoint
Only a Purview Audit search can inspect malware on that host

communityTop.text: Defender for Endpoint can remotely initiate a Microsoft Defender Antivirus scan even when another antivirus solution is present and Defender Antivirus is operating in passive mode. The responder can choose the supported scan type and track the action in Defender. Removing the device from Defender or switching to Purview would reduce response capability rather than enable the requested malware scan.

text: A responder exports Microsoft Purview Audit search results to CSV and needs to sort on individual event properties that are embedded inside the AuditData column. What is the recommended next processing step?

choices.text: Transform the AuditData JSON into separate columns
Rename AuditData to SecurityEvent before importing the file
Convert every audit record into a Sentinel incident
Hash the AuditData value and group by the resulting digest

communityTop.text: In Purview Audit exports, AuditData contains additional event information as a JSON object. Microsoft recommends using a JSON transform, such as Power Query's JSON transformation, to split those properties into separate columns so investigators can sort and filter on them. Renaming the column, creating incidents for every record, or hashing the JSON would discard or obscure the detail needed for investigation.

text: An investigator runs a Microsoft Purview eDiscovery search and wants a quick sense of how much content matched, which locations hold most of it, and examples of the returned items before exporting the full results. Which search outputs provide that view?

choices.text: Search statistics and a representative sample
Defender XDR evidence verdicts and remediation status
Microsoft Graph response codes and request URIs
Defender for Endpoint device-timeline process trees

communityTop.text: After an eDiscovery search runs, Microsoft Purview can show search statistics such as estimated item count, total size, and which content locations contain the most matches, along with a representative sample of matching items. Those outputs let an investigator validate and refine the search before export. Defender evidence, Graph request telemetry, and endpoint process trees describe different investigative data.

text: A responder is hunting suspicious Microsoft Graph API activity and needs to identify both the resource path that was requested and whether the API returned an authorization failure. Which TWO MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs fields directly provide those details?

communityTop.text: RequestUri records the URI targeted by the Microsoft Graph API request, while ResponseStatusCode records the HTTP status returned by the service, including authorization failures such as 401 or 403. DurationMs and ResponseSizeBytes describe performance and payload size, and Location identifies the region serving the request. Those fields can add context, but they do not directly answer the requested path-and-outcome pair.

text: A threat hunter suspects DLL side-loading on Windows endpoints and needs to identify which libraries were loaded by suspicious processes. Which Advanced Hunting table is the most appropriate starting point?

communityTop.text: DeviceImageLoadEvents records DLL loading activity on endpoints, making it the direct table for investigating which libraries a process loaded. DeviceNetworkInfo describes adapter and network configuration, while IdentityLogonEvents records authentication activity. EmailAttachmentInfo concerns files attached to email rather than modules loaded into endpoint processes.

text: An analyst is hunting for repeated interactive and remote logons to a specific workstation and wants endpoint authentication events tied to that device. Which table best fits the hunt?

communityTop.text: DeviceLogonEvents contains user logons and other authentication events observed on devices, so it is the appropriate endpoint-focused source for this hunt. DeviceProcessEvents tracks process creation, and DeviceFileEvents tracks file-system activity. CloudAppEvents focuses on account and object activity in cloud apps rather than logons occurring on the workstation itself.

text: A hunter finds a device communicating through an unexpected interface and needs the adapter name, MAC address, assigned IP addresses, DNS servers, and connected network information. Which Advanced Hunting table provides that configuration context?

communityTop.text: DeviceNetworkInfo describes network configuration for devices, including adapters, MAC addresses, IP addresses, DNS information, gateways, and connected networks. DeviceNetworkEvents records connections rather than the adapter configuration itself. DeviceInfo gives broader machine inventory details, while DeviceEvents contains miscellaneous security-control and device events.

text: A hunter wants authentication evidence that can include on-premises Active Directory activity captured by Defender for Identity as well as authentication activity from Microsoft online services. Which table should be queried?

communityTop.text: IdentityLogonEvents combines identity authentication activity from sources such as Defender for Identity and Microsoft online services, making it useful for cross-identity logon hunting. DeviceLogonEvents is endpoint-centric, while IdentityQueryEvents records queries against directory objects. CloudAppEvents records broader activity in cloud apps and is not the dedicated identity-authentication table.

text: A phishing hunt starts from a suspicious email. The analyst needs to identify the URLs contained in the message and determine whether recipients later clicked those links through Safe Links. Which TWO Advanced Hunting tables directly provide those two views?

communityTop.text: EmailUrlInfo provides information about URLs present in email messages, while UrlClickEvents records Safe Links click activity from email, Teams, and supported Microsoft 365 experiences. Together they let the hunter connect message content to subsequent user clicks. EmailAttachmentInfo concerns attachments, and the device-network and identity-query tables do not supply those two email-link views.

text: A campaign uses the same malicious attachment name across many messages. The hunter wants attachment filenames, file types, and available file hashes from Defender for Office 365 telemetry. Which table is designed for this data?

communityTop.text: EmailAttachmentInfo contains metadata about files attached to messages processed by Defender for Office 365, including filename, file type, size, threat verdict information, and available hashes. EmailEvents describes message processing and delivery, while AlertEvidence concerns entities attached to alerts. DeviceFileEvents records endpoint file-system activity after a file reaches a device.

text: A junior analyst understands the hunting goal but is not yet comfortable writing Kusto Query Language from scratch. Which Advanced Hunting mode is intended to let the analyst build the hunt by selecting filters and conditions instead?

communityTop.text: Guided mode is intended for analysts who prefer a query builder or are not yet comfortable authoring KQL directly. Advanced mode exposes the KQL editor for queries written from scratch. Graph and Detection are not the two hunting-authoring modes Microsoft documents for this choice, although graphs and detections can be used elsewhere in the investigation workflow.

text: A threat hunter has a useful Advanced Hunting query that every analyst in the same tenant should be able to find and run from the portal. Where should the query be saved?

communityTop.text: Saving the query under Shared queries makes it available to other users in the organization, which is the purpose of that location. My queries keeps a saved query private to its creator. Favorites helps with personal navigation, and a browser bookmark can preserve a page link but does not publish the query into the tenant's shared hunting library.

text: Several hunts repeat the same normalization and enrichment logic with different input values. The team wants that query logic to be reusable with parameters instead of copying it into every hunt. Which Advanced Hunting feature best fits?

communityTop.text: A custom function packages reusable Advanced Hunting query logic and can accept parameters, which avoids copying the same logic into every query. A bookmark preserves interesting hunting results rather than query logic. Summary rules aggregate data on a schedule, while incident tasks standardize response work and do not create reusable KQL components.

text: An Advanced Hunting query returns a Timestamp column. Without adding charting code, which visualization does the results experience automatically render to help the hunter spot bursts and unusual trends over time?

choices.text: A process tree for every row

communityTop.text: Advanced Hunting automatically renders a timeline above results when the output contains Timestamp or timeGenerated, showing event counts over time and updating as filters change. That helps a hunter spot spikes and focus on interesting periods. Graph paths, process trees, and geographic maps require different data and investigation experiences rather than appearing automatically from any timestamped result set.

text: A hunter needs to keep the existing columns in a result set and add a new calculated field named AccountKey built from other columns. Which KQL operator is designed for that task?

communityTop.text: The extend operator adds one or more calculated columns while retaining the other input columns, so it fits creation of AccountKey without rebuilding the whole projection. distinct reduces rows to unique combinations, summarize performs aggregation, and project-away removes selected columns. Those operators solve different shaping problems and do not simply append the requested calculated field.

text: A query returns thousands of authentication events, but the hunter only wants the unique combinations of AccountUpn and DeviceName that appear in the results. Which KQL operator is the most direct choice?

communityTop.text: distinct returns the unique combinations of the columns supplied to it, which directly answers the need for unique AccountUpn and DeviceName pairs. extend creates calculated columns, sort changes row order, and take limits the number of returned rows. None of those alternatives removes duplicates based on the selected pair of values.

text: A hunter groups events by source IP and wants an efficient estimate of how many different user accounts each IP attempted to authenticate as. Which KQL aggregation function best matches that requirement?

communityTop.text: dcount() estimates the number of distinct values in a column, so it is suited to counting different accounts associated with each source IP. count() counts rows regardless of whether the same account repeats. make_list() collects values into an array, while arg_max() returns the row associated with a maximum expression rather than a distinct-value estimate.

text: While reviewing a hunting graph, an analyst selects a suspicious device and wants to reveal the next set of assets related to that node so the investigation can move outward from the initial result. Which graph action supports this?

communityTop.text: Explore connected assets expands the selected node so the analyst can traverse additional relationships beyond the initial graph results. This is the graph-native action for moving outward through connected entities. Summary rules and analytics-tier promotion are data-processing features, while saving a shared query preserves KQL but does not expand relationships from a graph node.

text: An identity hunter wants to determine which paths a compromised account could use through role assignments and group memberships to reach a critical Azure resource. Which capability is best suited to this relationship-heavy question?

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel Graph models entities and their relationships, and identity attack graph scenarios can expose lateral-movement and privilege paths from identities to resources. A workbook can visualize query results but does not itself model those graph relationships. Action center manages response actions, and a Purview Audit export provides event records rather than path analysis across connected identities and resources.

text: A team begins a proactive investigation with a written hypothesis and wants to record whether the hypothesis is validated, keep investigation notes, and track analytic rules or incidents created from the findings. Which Sentinel construct is designed for that workflow?

communityTop.text: A Microsoft Sentinel hunt is designed around a hunting hypothesis and lets analysts investigate related queries, record results and comments, and track whether the hypothesis was validated. Hunts also link analytic rules and incidents created from the investigation. Workbooks visualize data, automation rules orchestrate incident actions, and data collection rules control ingestion rather than managing a hunting hypothesis.

text: During a Sentinel hunt, an analyst bookmarks a suspicious event and later determines that the evidence is severe enough to require formal investigation by the incident-response queue. What should the analyst do with that bookmarked finding?

choices.text: Escalate the bookmark to an incident
Convert it to a data connector
Move it to a custom log table
Turn it into an ingestion transformation

communityTop.text: Microsoft Sentinel hunting bookmarks preserve notable findings, and a bookmarked event that warrants investigation can be escalated into an incident. That turns a hunting lead into a formal response case while retaining the investigative context. Data connectors, custom log tables, and ingestion transformations change how data is collected or stored and are unrelated to escalating a specific hunting finding.

text: A hunter needs to investigate long-retained Sentinel data and run a complex query that joins several tables before persisting useful results for further analysis. Which TWO characteristics make a Data lake KQL job appropriate?

choices.text: It can query historical data retained for up to 12 years
It supports complex KQL such as joins and unions across tables
It is optimized for hydrating results from one source table
It queries the analytics tier without data lake onboarding
It uses the restricted operator set associated with search jobs

communityTop.text: KQL jobs are intended for investigation over Microsoft Sentinel data lake data, including long historical lookback of up to 12 years and complex KQL operations such as joins or unions across multiple tables. They can run on demand or on a schedule and write results to the analytics tier. Single-table-only behavior is associated with search jobs, not KQL jobs, and KQL jobs do not require the source to begin in the analytics tier.

text: A SOC wants a background aggregation every 20 minutes over high-volume Basic-tier firewall data, and the workspace is not onboarded to the Sentinel data lake. Which feature is the better fit?

communityTop.text: Summary rules are built for frequent background aggregation and can work with data such as Basic or Auxiliary tier logs even when the workspace is not onboarded to the Sentinel data lake. KQL jobs require data lake onboarding and are better for historical or more complex investigation queries. Bookmarks preserve hunting findings, while Live Response is an endpoint-response capability rather than a log-aggregation mechanism.

text: A threat-hunting notebook needs reusable security-focused Python capabilities for querying data, enrichment, anomaly detection, and visualization. Which package is specifically designed for this use in Microsoft Sentinel notebooks?

communityTop.text: MSTICPy is Microsoft's security-focused Python library used with Microsoft Sentinel notebooks for data retrieval, enrichment, analysis, anomaly detection, and visualization. General-purpose libraries can still be useful inside a notebook, but MSTICPy supplies reusable investigation and hunting functionality designed for security workflows. OpenSSL and PowerShellGet solve unrelated cryptography and package-management tasks.
